newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up on rebound.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended higher on Monday on a technical rebound after sharp falls last week, traders said.
The most actively traded September contract rose 20 yuan to 3,310 yuan ($399). It opened at an intraday low of 3,300 yuan and hit a high of 3,312 yuan in late trading.
July rose 22 to 3,252, November six yuan to 3,302 January 1998 nine yuan to 3,311 and March five yuan to 3,216.
Combined volume rose to 15,500 tonnes from 10,500.
Traders said some long-position holders began to buy after falls last week, pushing up the prices today.

"But short-positions holders did not cover their positions, believing prices cannot go up solidly in the short term," one trader said. "The market widely expects they will launch attacks to depress prices on Tuesday."
But most traders said they believed there was a rough balance of supply and demand on the market and that the prices were likely to move in a narrow range around the current level in the near term.
